newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Todd will say NZ Super unsustainable - Peters.
newsitem.headline: Todd will say NZ Super unsustainable - Peters.

text.p: Treasurer Winston Peters on Wednesday predicted that the Todd task force will say in its interim report on superannuation due on Thursday that the current pension scheme is unsustainable.
"I predict that it will show that New Zealand Super is not sustainable in its current form," Peters told the Mount Victoria Rotary Club.
"That is, there will need to be substantial change to the taxation rates, payment levels, or eligibility criteria if New Zealand Super is to continue," he said.
Peters also said the accord on New Zealand Super was dead.
"It barely lasted three years before the Alliance (Party) walked away by promising progressive taxes, and Labour a dedicated tax and fund."
Peters said New Zealand Super could only be sustained if taxes were raised, benefits were cut or eligibility changed.
He said the Todd report was likely to suggest small changes on a number of fronts.
"It is unlikely however, to spell out what these small changes should be or what combination of changes need to occur
"It is also likely to reintroduce the surtax as a lever that could be used to make New Zealand Super sustainable."
